title: fix: gnomad chr prefix disables the lowercase-allele repair
description:
The `gnomad` source accepts an optional `chr` prefix, and separately repairs a
lowercase allele to uppercase. The two do not compose: adding the prefix
silently disables the repair.

## Current behavior

| Input | Valid | Suggestion |
|---|---|---|
| `1-55516888-g-a` | `FALSE` | `1-55516888-G-A` |
| `chr1-55516888-g-a` | `FALSE` | none |
| `CHR1-55516888-G-A` | `FALSE` | none |

R and Python agree exactly, so this is not a parity break and the conformance
corpus passes. The verdict is also correct in every row: none of these are
valid gnomAD identifiers. Only the repair hint is missing.

## Cause

`shared/sources/gnomad.yaml` opens the pattern with a lowercase literal:

```
pattern: '(?:chr)?(?:[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-2]|X|Y|MT?)-[0-9]+-[ACGTN]+-[ACGTN]+'
normalize:
  case: upper
```

The `case: upper` rule uppercases the whole string before re-matching, in
`pkg-py/src/biobouncer/_pattern.py` and the matching branch in
`pkg-r/R/mode-pattern.R`. So `chr1-55516888-g-a` becomes `CHR1-55516888-G-A`,
which no longer matches `(?:chr)?`, and no candidate is produced.

## Why the obvious fix is not enough

Making the prefix case-insensitive, for example `(?:[Cc][Hh][Rr])?` to stay
safe across PCRE and Python `re`, makes the input repairable but produces
`CHR1-55516888-G-A` as the suggestion. Uppercase `CHR` is not the canonical
gnomAD spelling, so the suggestion would be worse than none.

A proper fix needs a normalize rule that targets the allele fields rather than
the whole string, which the schema does not currently express. Options worth
weighing:

* Add a field-scoped normalize rule to `shared/schema/`, which is the general
  fix and would help any future coordinate-style source.
* Special-case the prefix the way `_ensembl_id_prefix` already special-cases
  Ensembl species codes in `_pattern.py`, which is narrower but cheaper.
* Decide the combination is out of scope and document it, since `chr` plus
  lowercase alleles is an uncommon pairing in real data.

## Corpus cases to add once the behavior is decided

```json
{"input": "chr1-55516888-g-a", "source_db": "gnomad", "how": "pattern", "expect": {"valid": false, "suggestion": "chr1-55516888-G-A"}, "note": "a chr prefix does not block the lowercase-allele repair"}
{"input": "CHR1-55516888-G-A", "source_db": "gnomad", "how": "pattern", "expect": {"valid": false, "suggestion": "chr1-55516888-G-A"}, "note": "an uppercase chr prefix is repairable to the canonical lowercase form"}
```

The expected suggestions above assume lowercase `chr` is chosen as canonical.
Adjust them to match whichever option is taken.

## Not affected

No shipped vignette, example or README references `gnomad`, and the CRAN
submission is unaffected. Found while reviewing #88.

title: Add a variant-coordinate id source (gnomAD-style chr-pos-ref-alt, VCF, SPDI)
description:
## Summary

Add an id source for **genomic variant coordinates** (gnomAD-style
`chrom-pos-ref-alt`, and ideally VCF and SPDI), so raw coordinate identifiers can
be validated through the same `check_id()` / `id_predicate()` seam as everything
else.

## Motivation

The package description is "validate gene symbols, ontology terms, **variant
formats**, and database identifiers". Today the variant-format coverage is `hgvs`
(plus `dbsnp`, `clinvar`), but there is no source for a raw genomic coordinate:

```r
biobouncer::check_id("1-55516888-G-A", "gnomad")   # no such source
biobouncer::check_id("17-7676154-G-C", "opentargets")$valid   # FALSE
```

Coordinate ids are one of the most common variant "formats" in practice: gnomAD
variant ids, VCF-derived `chr-pos-ref-alt`, and SPDI are how most pipelines key
variants once identity is resolved.

## Where this bit

In `multi-variant-reviewer` every variant is keyed on a gnomAD-style
`chrom-pos-ref-alt` string. Those keys are sometimes **synthesised** from an
upstream coordinate response (e.g. ClinGen Allele Registry), and a deletion came
back with an empty allele, producing a malformed key (`7-117559594-CTT-`) that a
downstream coordinate client then choked on. biobouncer could not gate that key
because it has no coordinate source, so the check that "every external/derived id
crosses one validation seam" had a hole exactly where a coordinate is formed.
(The downstream crash is our bug and is fixed on our side; this issue is about
closing the validation gap so the seam is complete.)

## Proposed

One or more sources, e.g.:

- `gnomad` (or `variant` / `vcf`): `chrom-pos-ref-alt`, dash-delimited, e.g.
  `1-55516888-G-A`, `X-149481232-TG-T`.
- `spdi`: `sequence:position:deletion:insertion`, e.g.
  `NC_000001.11:55516887:G:A`.

Validation should reject the failure modes that actually cause silent downstream
breakage:

- an empty ref or alt (the gnomAD form requires both present),
- a non-numeric position,
- non-ACGTN alleles (allowing `N`),
- a missing field / wrong delimiter count.

A `repair_id()` path (e.g. normalising `chr1` -> `1`, uppercasing alleles) would
be a bonus but is not required for the core ask.

## Context

Filed from building `multi-variant-reviewer`, which would route its synthesised
coordinate keys through `check_id(key, "gnomad", how = "pattern")` as the single
offline validation seam if the source existed. Checked against biobouncer 0.1.3
(current on samuelbharti.r-universe.dev).

title: hgnc: a lowercase gene symbol gets no suggestion, or the wrong gene
description:
## What happens

A lowercase gene symbol is one of the most common forms of messy input in real
data. biobouncer currently handles none of them, and for a few it suggests a
different gene.

Tried 19 common symbols in lowercase against the pinned `hgnc` snapshot
(`check_id(s, source_db="hgnc", how="cache")`). **0 of 19 produced the right
answer.**

Suggested the wrong gene:

| input | suggested | correct |
|---|---|---|
| `tp53` | `CD53` | `TP53` |
| `rb1` | `AK1` | `RB1` |
| `il6` | `AK6` | `IL6` |

No suggestion at all (16): `brca1`, `brca2`, `egfr`, `kras`, `myc`, `pten`,
`akt1`, `vhl`, `apc`, `met`, `ret`, `alk`, `erbb2`, `tnf`, `gapdh`, `actb`.

R and Python agree exactly, including on the wrong genes, so this is not a parity
break. The conformance corpus is doing its job; it just never had a case for
this.

```r
check_id(c("tp53", "rb1", "brca1"), source_db = "hgnc", how = "cache")
#>   input valid suggestion
#> 1  tp53 FALSE       CD53
#> 2   rb1 FALSE        AK1
#> 3 brca1 FALSE       <NA>
```

## Why

`hgnc` has no `curie` or `normalize` rule, which is correct: a gene symbol has no
prefix to fold and no single case convention. So a case-only difference never
gets repaired on the normalize path, and falls through to the fuzzy fallback
(`shared/sources/hgnc.yaml`, `suggest.fuzzy.max_distance: 2`).

Fuzzy matching is case-sensitive Levenshtein, so every wrong-case character spends
one edit from a budget of 2:

- `tp53` -> `TP53` is distance 2, and `tp53` -> `CD53` is also distance 2. It is a
  tie, broken deterministically by codepoint, and `C` (0x43) sorts before `T`
  (0x54). The wrong gene wins.
- `brca1` -> `BRCA1` is distance 4, over the budget, so nothing is returned. Any
  symbol of 3+ lowercase letters is out of reach for the same reason.

The comment in `hgnc.yaml` says the intent was typo correction ("a typo like TP52
suggests TP53"). Case was not part of the design, and the fallback silently
inherited it.

## Suggested fix

Try a case-insensitive exact match against the approved-symbol set **before**
falling back to fuzzy. A case-only difference is not a guess, it is a known
answer, and it should not compete with real neighbours on edit distance.

Rough shape: build a casefold -> approved map alongside the id set when a
snapshot is loaded, and consult it in the suggestion path ahead of the fuzzy
call. It fits where the retired-map lookup already sits: retired map, then
case-insensitive exact, then fuzzy.

**Do not do this with a `normalize: case: upper` rule.** 263 of the 45,019
approved symbols in the pinned snapshot are not all-uppercase (`C9orf72` is in
the bundled `sample`), so uppercasing would corrupt them. A case-insensitive
lookup returns the snapshot's own spelling and handles `c9orf72` -> `C9orf72`
correctly.

Whether the result should be `valid=TRUE` or `valid=FALSE` with a suggestion is
worth deciding explicitly. Suggestion-only is the conservative option and matches
how `mondo:5148` -> `MONDO:0005148` behaves today.

## Files

- `pkg-py/src/biobouncer/_cache.py:182` `_fuzzy_fallback`, and `pkg-r/R/cache.R:177`
- `pkg-py/src/biobouncer/_fuzzy.py`, `pkg-r/R/fuzzy.R`
- `shared/sources/hgnc.yaml` if the behaviour becomes configurable
- `shared/corpus/hgnc.cases.jsonl` for the cases that would have caught this

Both languages must land together with corpus cases, per the parity rule.

Found while verifying README examples for the 0.1.1 PyPI release (#61). Not
shipped as a regression: the behaviour predates that work.
